newsitem.title: SPAIN: Popular shares gain on consumer pick-up.
newsitem.headline: Popular shares gain on consumer pick-up.

text.p: Shares in Banco Popular outpaced the Spanish stock market on Friday, bolstered by switching from other banks amid expectations that it would benefit from a consumption pick-up, dealers said.

At 1030 GMT, Popular was 1,010 pesetas, or 2.87 percent, ahead at 36,200 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was down 0.58 percent to 6,891.45. A large put through earlier today also boosted trade in Popular.

An expected rise in private consumption was driving the shares on forecasts that Popular, having the largest retail presence among the banks, would benefit from a consequent increase in consumer lending, analysts said.
A dealer who asked not to be named said he had seen switching into Popular out of Santander and Banco Bilbao Vizcaya.
One analyst said switching would be logical, although he could not confirm whether switches were taking place.

"Popular is the bank with most retail presence, and an increase in consumption favours it...as long as that rise is translated into more demand for credit," said Juan de Dios, analyst at Ahorro Corporacion Financiera.
"I think it's reasonable investors who've seen a rise of around 70 percent in Santander and BBV would move into Popular, which has less upside potential, but less risk," he added.

Popular is also relatively cheap compared to its peers. The ACF analyst said the bank is trading on a prospective price-earnings ratio (PE) of 15 times his forecast of 1997 profits, versus 21 times for BBV and 20.7 for Santander.
